subject: Post-call: performance needs & integration checklist — CovePay
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@covepay.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@covepay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-18 14:05 PDT
Subject: Post-call: performance needs & integration checklist — CovePay

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation. I wanted to capture the key constraints we heard and propose a lightweight integration checklist so we can scope the technical deep-dive next week. TL;DR: your top priorities are predictable tail latency during settlement spikes, SOC2 evidence for procurement, and a low-friction integration for embeddings + alert generation.

Recap of pain points you shared:
- Severe tail latency spikes during 2x/day settlement windows (affects fraud scoring and customer-facing alerts).
- Bursty throughput: baseline ~400–800 RPS; peak windows commonly hit 1.2k–1.8k RPS for 15–40 minutes.
- Two primary workloads: semantic embeddings (search/matching) and short generation (alert text, risk summary). Embeddings are ~70% of calls by volume, generation is more latency-sensitive.
- Compliance: SOC2 and US data residency are hard requirements for production.

Proposed SLO targets (please confirm these are aligned with your goals):
- Embedding path: p50 <= 25ms, p95 <= 75ms, p99 <= 200ms for 512-dim embeddings (active index + cache).
- Generation path (interactive alerts): p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 160ms, p99 <= 400ms, max token length ~256.
- Throughput: sustain 1.5k RPS with headroom for 2k RPS spikes for up to 40 minutes.

Initial deployment topology (recommendation):
1) Staging: Hosted Redwood API (us-west) for dev + integration tests.
2) Production: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with private control plane (VPC). Rationale: dedicated pools give predictable tail behavior and data isolation required by procurement.
3) Data plane optimizations: KV cache for repeated contexts, prefix caching for templates, and continuous batching on background embedding jobs. For interactive generation, use small batch sizes + concurrency limits to preserve p95/p99.
4) Model guidance: start with a quantized 13B-class model for the generation pipeline (better latency/cost tradeoff) and higher-throughput smaller embedding model (7B) or optimized embedding model we maintain. We can validate with a short sweep.

Short-term asks / next steps:
- Confirm the SLO targets above (or tell us which to reprioritize).
- Permission to share SOC2 summary + Docs with your security team.
- If agreed, we'll run a quick throughput simulation (our infra team) against a small mirror of your traffic pattern and follow up with a short cost comparison: hosted vs. dedicated reserved + burst.
- Proposed time for technical deep-dive: Tue 2028-04-25 or Wed 2028-04-26; propose 10:00–11:30 PT.

I'll attach a one-page mutual action plan and SOC2 summary in my next email. If you want a different breakdown of latencies (e.g., p90 instead of p95), let me know.

—
Rishi Malhotra

- Confirming priorities: p99 latency during settlement windows is our top non-functional requirement, then SOC2 evidence for procurement, then cost predictability.
- Peak traffic: those 1.2k–1.8k spikes are accurate and usually last 20–35 minutes; they happen twice a day (med/pm batch).

Also please share a simple topology diagram we can circulate with our architecture team — the diagram will help our procurement folks understand data plane residency and control plane boundaries.

If Tuesday 4/25 is proposed, 10:00 PT works for me.

Thanks Daniel — noted and great to confirm the priorities. Quick answers + attachments below.

Ballpark monthly ranges (order-of-magnitude, for budgeting only):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): $14k–$28k / month — depends on sustained counts vs spikes; embeddings-heavy workloads push this toward the upper end unless aggressive prefix caching is enabled.
- Dedicated (1yr reserved + burst): baseline reserved ~ $11k–$15k / month (committed capacity sized to sustain 1.5k RPS) + burst usage billed at lower incremental rates. Dedicated reduces variance and improves p99 predictability; we can firm numbers after a short capacity simulation.

Attachments included: covepay-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP milestones + owners), redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (high-level evidence + contact for SOC2 audit). Also shared a simple topology diagram to the Drive link in my first note.

Short technical notes:
- For the embedding path we recommend a background batching pipeline (large batches) that writes vectors to your index. Use a separate, autoscaled pool for embeddings; caching at the frontend layer (LRU) buys large p99 improvements for repeated queries.
- For the alert generation path, use a low-latency dedicated pool with small batch size and KV cache warmup for frequent templates. Avoid aggressive batching on the interactive path — it increases tail latency.
- Quantization: for the generation model we expect int8/int4 quantization will reduce per-token latency ~1.6x–2.2x depending on model. We'll validate across 7B/13B model options.

Next steps I will action:
1) Run a 2-hour throughput simulation that mirrors your peak window (we'll need a 24–48hr access window to a sample traffic trace — or we can replay a synthetic trace you provide).
2) Produce a short hosted vs dedicated cost comparison with p99 sensitivity analysis.
3) Schedule the technical deep-dive Tuesday 2028-04-25 10:00–11:30 PT (calendar invite to follow).

If that's all good I will send the M.A.P. and SOC2 doc now (attached).

—
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
